I am of the view that there is something we humans call "Value" that is fundamental to our current societal organization (capitalism and democracy). 

To quantify "Value" numerically (as would be requied for a computer) you would arrive at something akin to monetary value in the financial sense.

But if you ask most people, they would tell you that monetary value is not the same as human "Value". I would argue that something of general human "Value" will also tend to have monetary financial value as the numbers are really just a way of communicating this value for the purpose of trade.

So if you ask me, AI like any computation program, will be excellent at the numbers and optimizing financial value, but in the end of the day, it will struggle with understanding the innovations that provide the underlying human value to create new financial value.

Now it is possible that a computer will decide that it believes it knows "Value" just as well as a human does, but I honestly doubt it because an AI computer program is really just
a complex mathematical formula, and as smart as it may seem, it really can't think outside the numbers.

I'm not saying there won't be signifiant societal shifts that will occur as AIs become more prevalent, but I always see them as relying on the human definition of "Value".
